subject: Request: Transitional billing bridge (Net-60 -> Quarterly hybrid) — approval needed
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Park <jenna.park@procureops.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-07T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Proposal: Transitional billing bridge (Net-60 -> Quarterly hybrid) — details attached

Hi Jenna,

Thanks for the call this morning — appreciate the transparency on CareTX’s procurement timing. As discussed, procurement needs an initial Net-60 invoice cadence for the first two quarters while their budget cycle shifts to a quarterly remit in Q2. To keep the pilot live and preserve our go-live target (Dec 1), the deal desk proposed a temporary hybrid billing bridge: Redwood invoices Net-60 for Q1 and Q2, then transitions to quarterly consolidated invoices starting Q3, accompanied by a one-time onboarding credit to offset the deferred cashflow impact.

I’ve attached a one-page proposed billing schedule and the SOW mark-up (proposed_billing_schedule_v1.pdf, SOW_CareTX_Redwood_v1.docx). Key ask for CareTX: confirmation that Net-60 for two quarters is acceptable and procurement sign-off on the quarterly transition. Our ask to Redwood leadership: approval to accept the temporary Net-60 window and to provide a one-time onboarding credit of $25,000 (applied across first two invoices) conditioned on the signed SOW and a commitment to the 12-month term.

Proposed summary: 
- Term: 12 months
- Pilot billing: Net-60 for invoices issued in Dec 2026 and Feb 2027 (two invoice cycles)
- Transition: Quarterly consolidated invoices starting May 2027
- One-time onboarding credit: $25,000 applied against the first two invoices

Reason: preserves go-live cadence, keeps revenue recognized under the contract, and avoids losing the customer to a one-quarter delay.

Can you please route this to your procurement and finance for confirmation? Marcus and Laura — looping you for deal desk / finance review and executive signoff if acceptable.

Thanks,

Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Lead, North America
Redwood Inference
(t) +1 415-555-0142
(tessa.morgan@redwood.ai)

Attachments: proposed_billing_schedule_v1.pdf, SOW_CareTX_Redwood_v1.docx

From: Jenna Park <jenna.park@procureops.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: CareTX AP <ap@caretx.com>
Date: 2026-11-07T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: Transitional billing bridge (Net-60 -> Quarterly hybrid) — details attached

Thanks Tessa — forwarding to our procurement and AP teams. A couple quick clarifications from my side before they commit: 1) the onboarding credit — will that be an invoice-level credit (reduces amounts due) or a service-credit applied later? 2) What assurances do we have that the quarterly consolidation will align with our fiscal quarters and not create double-counting for usage in the transition month?

AP has asked for a clear schedule with invoice dates and a short note on how usage will be prorated for any mid-quarter charge. If you can provide that in the proposed schedule PDF I can expedite signoff.

—Jenna
ProcureOps (on behalf of CareTX)
jenna.park@procureops.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-08T08:21:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: Transitional billing bridge (Net-60 -> Quarterly hybrid) — finance input / risk assessment

Team — reviewed CareTX’s ask and the proposed schedule. Short summary for execs: this is a revenue-timing shift (we'll bill later for two cycles), estimated cashflow impact ~$210k spread over two billing cycles (based on ARR and expected usage). The onboarding credit is a commercial concession to mitigate their cash flow pain; given the size of the account (expected ARR $1.9M), $25k is acceptable from a commercial ROI standpoint.

Risks: 
- Cashflow: temporary DSO increase for two months; we can cover via reserves but should track closely.
- Precedent: approving Net-60 + credit sets an example for other enterprise prospects. We should attach an explicit clause that this is a one-time, non-precedent-setting exception tied to CareTX’s procurement timing.

Requesting: executive approval for 1) temporary Net-60 for two invoice cycles, 2) $25k onboarding credit, 3) clause language limiting precedent. I recommend vp-level signoff (Jonas) so legal/finance can finalize contract language quickly.

Marcus Lin
Head of Deal Desk, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-10T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: Transitional billing bridge (Net-60 -> Quarterly hybrid) — APPROVED (conditional)

I approve the temporary Net-60 bridge for two invoice cycles and the $25,000 onboarding credit as a conditional, one-off concession for CareTX (DEAL-7421). Conditions before contract execution: 
1) Legal to insert explicit non-precedent language and a reversion clause to standard quarterly billing after Q2 2027.
2) Finance to confirm cashflow monitoring plan and escalation point if DSO grows beyond modeled $210k impact.
3) Sales (Tessa) to obtain a written procurement commitment from CareTX confirming the quarterly transition and a signed SOW referencing the billing schedule.

Once legal and finance confirm the conditions are met, Laura please mark the deal as "Approved — Transitional Billing" in HubSpot and attach the final SOW.

Jonas Weber
VP, Commercial Operations
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
